methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective case series of only 6 consecutive relapsed/refractory RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML patients receiving a novel olaparib-augmented myeloablative conditioning regimen for allo-HSCT. Treatment protocol is described in detail (olaparib 150 mg bid days -15 to -4, FLAG, busulfan, cyclophosphamide), with serial MRD monitoring by RQ-PCR and standardized aGVHD/cGVHD criteria. However, n=6 with no control group precludes any inferential analysis; there are essentially no statistics beyond descriptive summaries. Patient heterogeneity is substantial: varying co-mutations (KIT, FLT3, BCORL1, CSF3R, TET2, ASXL, BRCA2), different donor types (5 haploidentical + 1 matched sibling), and mixed active-disease/CR2+ status at transplant. No formal survival analysis is possible with 6 patients at 25 months follow-up.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series of 6 patients maps to Oxford LoE 4. The rationale (RUNX1::RUNX1T1 sensitizes to PARPi via HRR suppression, ref 5) is biologically plausible, and all 6 patients achieved CMR by 3 months with 100% LFS at 25 months median follow-up — encouraging if reproducible. However, the small sample and selected, heavily pretreated population mean the finding is hypothesis-generating for a prospective trial rather than directly changing practice.

reporting_quality.justification: This is most appropriately a case series; CARE guidelines would apply but are not in the schema enum, hence 'other'. The manuscript describes conditioning dosing, engraftment times, MRD monitoring schedule, and GVHD/viral complications individually by UPN, which supports transparency. However, there is no data availability statement, no CONSORT/STROBE/CARE checklist, no supplementary individual patient tables shown in-text, and minor grammatical issues (e.g., 'AML with positive has shown to have clinical heterogeneity', 'Age14 to 60 years old'). Ethics approval is reported.

novelty_literature.justification: This is described as the first case series of allo-HSCT using an olaparib-containing conditioning regimen specifically for relapsed/refractory RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML. The biological rationale (synthetic lethality via HRR suppression in RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ leukemia per Esposito et al. 2015, ref 5) plus the mechanistic link to NKG2D ligand induction on LSCs and NK-cell-mediated clearance represents a genuinely novel translational concept. The authors' prior work on olaparib + chemotherapy in elderly RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML (ref 16) and olaparib in T-ALL (ref 14) establishes a continuous research program.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally understandable with a clear treatment protocol description and patient-by-patient narrative. However, several grammatical errors and dropped words exist: 'AML with the t(8;21)... is generally associated with a favorable outcome, but AML with positive has shown to have clinical heterogeneity', 'Age14 to 60 years old', 'one of whom concurrently exhibited of the central nervous system leukemia'. The Discussion is proportionate and the mechanistic rationale is coherent, but the limitations statement is brief.

key_strengths: Novel translational concept: first allo-HSCT conditioning regimen incorporating olaparib for relapsed/refractory RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML, grounded in documented synthetic-lethality biology (Esposito et al. 2015)
All 6 patients achieved CMR by 3 months and 100% LFS at 25 months median follow-up, despite half being in active disease and none in CR1 at transplant
Detailed conditioning protocol, engraftment metrics (median neutrophil/platelet engraftment 15 days), and standardized GVHD/viral complication reporting
Coherent mechanistic discussion linking PARPi to NKG2D ligand induction and NK/T-cell-mediated LSC clearance post-transplant
key_concerns: n=6 with no control group precludes any inferential efficacy or safety conclusions; chronic GVHD occurred in 100% and CMV/EBV reactivation in 4/6
Heterogeneous population (mixed haploidentical vs matched sibling donors, mixed active disease vs CR2+, diverse co-mutations)
No data/code availability statement; no CARE or other case-series checklist declared
Grammatical errors and dropped words affecting clarity ('AML with positive', 'Age14 to 60')
Findings are hypothesis-generating only; prospective randomized or single-arm multi-center trials are needed
chief_reviewer.rationale: A novel, biologically-rationalized case series of only 6 patients with striking 100% early CMR and 25-month LFS in a heavily pretreated RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML population; promising hypothesis-generating signal but severely underpowered. Best fits a tier 3 specialty hematology/oncology journal after major revisions to address writing polish, reporting checklist, and explicit acknowledgment of inferential limits.
